name: Clothra

attributes.attribute: one of the four noted daughters of Eochaid Fedlech

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Clothra, also called Clothru, was an Irish heroine or goddess. The legendary king Eochaid Fedlech had four noted daughters, Medb, Eithne, Mugain, and Clothra, and three sons, all named Finn. Clothra bore a single son to her three brothers, each of them fathering a lawful part of his body marked by red stripes. That son was Lugaidh Riab nDerg. She then lay with her son and conceived the hero Crimthann Nia Náir, who was born after her death. Medb, her jealous sister, killed her. The line of incest hints at an ancestral deity.

okr.objective: Clothra is a heroine whose children, born from her brothers, trace an ancestral goddess.
key_results: Clothra is a daughter of king Eochaid Fedlech.
